limitation: Parked GPS jitter is counted as distance
scenario: fixtures/F_PARKED_JITTER.csv: parked 1 h inside Z1, 361 pings, each within 5 m of one point
consequence: advertiser billed, driver paid for not moving

limitation: Zig-zag inside the 100 m corridor is counted in full
scenario: 10 pings 0.0004 deg apart along R1 inside Z1, alternating 89 m either side of the road; 10/10 kept
consequence: no filter for lateral wander within 100 m

limitation: A 3-hour gap is bridged as one straight segment
scenario: ping at (0.0070, 0), next ping 3 h later at (0.0100, 0.0025); implied speed 0.145 km/h, so accepted
compared_with: shortest along-road route 0.611572 km; real route in 3 h unknown
consequence: unknown real distance replaced by a straight chord; no gap limit

limitation: A spike on the first ping becomes the speed anchor
scenario: first ping on R1's far end (0.0200, 0.005), then 10 normal pings inside Z1; 3 valid pings dropped as too fast
consequence: valid pings lost until the time gap makes the spike look reachable (A21)

limitation: A duplicate whose first copy is noise loses the good copy
scenario: ping 3 sent twice at the same second: first copy 167 m off road, second copy on R1 (corner); status first copy DROPPED_OFFROAD, good copy DUPLICATE
compared_with: 0.22239 km if the good copy were kept
consequence: A6 keeps the first copy, A3 then drops it; the corner is cut

limitation: A segment crossing local midnight goes wholly to the start day
scenario: fixtures/F_DAYCUT.csv DRV-B segment 14:59:55Z -> 15:00:05Z (0.044478 km inside Z1) is booked on 2026-11-07. In data/pings.csv 3 segments cross 00:00 UTC+9 (0.036539 km inside Z1) but all end exactly at 15:00:00Z, so their after-midnight share is 0.000000 km
compared_with: time-proportional share driven after midnight but booked on the previous day (A8)
consequence: by design under A8; the 10 s grid in data/pings.csv hides it

limitation: A (0,0) 'null island' ping lies on R1 and is never off-road
scenario: distance of (0,0) to R1 = 0.0 m; near R1's start the (0,0) ping is ACCEPTED; inside Z1 it is DROPPED_SPEED only by the speed filter
compared_with: any real GPS null fix would be kept if speed allows
consequence: R1 starts at (0,0); real routes rarely do

limitation: All geometry and tests sit at latitude 0
scenario: F_BOUNDARY, R1 and Z1 moved to lat 60 N: fixed.py 0.555975 km vs independent Liang-Barsky + haversine 0.555975 km (at lat 0: 0.778364 km)
compared_with: fixed.py vs independent calculation at lat 60
consequence: longitude scaling (cos lat) is never exercised by the test suite; only this measurement covers it

limitation: One bad row rejects the whole file
scenario: data/pings.csv with the Z removed from 1 of 2525 rows: rejected (1 problem), no output
compared_with: 2525 rows and 12 drivers held back by 1 row (A17)
consequence: safe (no wrong pay) but nobody is paid until the file is fixed

limitation: Late pings after the daily cut change a day already reported
scenario: DRV-03, local day 2026-11-07: its last 6 pings before 15:00Z arrive after the report is published; published 1.112762 km, after re-run 1.144128 km
compared_with: no restatement or versioning of a published day
consequence: batch re-run silently changes a closed day

limitation: qa_check can only judge km against generator ground truth
scenario: correct fixed.py output for data/pings.csv checked against a ground truth with no DAILY_KM rows: exit 1; daily rows compared: 15   tolerance: 0.001 km   failed: 15
compared_with: on real data there is no ground truth, so km cannot be verified this way
consequence: real-data QA needs another oracle (e.g. a second implementation or invariants)
